name: Neo-Mandaic
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Haberl, Charles G. 2009. The Neo-Mandaic Dialect of Khorramshahr. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz (full grammar with phonology incl. stress); no open copy reachable.

new_statements.quote: Word stress typically falls upon a tense vowel within a closed syllable. The placement of the stress is determined from the final syllable. Any final syllable (or ultima) that is closed and contains a tense vowel automatically receives the accent [...]. If the final is open or contains a lax vowel, the accent will fall upon the penultimate syllable, provided that it is closed or contains a tense vowel, e.g., kálbɔ ‘dog’. Otherwise, the stress will fall on the final syllable, e.g., dəmɔ́ ‘blood’ [...]. In words of three or more syllables, if neither the ultima nor the penultima is closed and contains a tense vowel, then the accent recedes to the antepenultimate syllable [...]

(1) text layer of the Knowledge Commons pre-publication proof of Häberl 2019 'Mandaic', Routledge Semitic Languages 2nd edn): the quoted passage is at the end of §3 Phonology on proof p. 687 (running head 'Mandaic 687', footer '...026-r03.indd 687'), immediately before '4 MORPHOLOGY'. The report's quote matches word for word; the three '[...]' elide only the examples (qə=mahrəwɔ́t 'you destroy'; bəġásˁ 'he stopped'; gatˁél-nɔ-χon 'I will kill you') and the closing sentence on lá. new_statements.rule_in_words: Right-edge, weight-sensitive stress within a three-syllable window, where 'heavy' = closed syllable and/or tense vowel (i, u, ɔ): a closed ultima with a tense vowel takes stress (qə=mahrəwɔ́t, Baġdɔ́d); otherwise the penult is stressed if it is closed or has a tense vowel (kálbɔ, gáwrɔ, éṯmal); in words of three or more syllables where neither ultima nor penult qualifies, stress goes to the antepenult (gaṭélnɔxon); if nothing qualifies (light disyllables), stress is final (dəmɔ́, əxál, qamɔ́, əháw). Häberl marks stress only where unpredictable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No explicit statement; phonetic transcriptions occasionally show a secondary mark (e.g. əmalfenanni [ə.ˌmal.fɛ.ˈnɑn.ni] 'we will teach him', 2019 p. 686; [ga.ˈtˤɛl.nɒ.ˌχon] in the Wikipedia rendering).
new_statements.exceptions: Certain morphemes are inherently stressed, notably the negative prefix lá-, which 'invariably carries the primary stress' and shifts stress to the first syllable of the verb (láhawlonni 'they didn't give him'); loanwords may retain source-language stress (aziyát 'distress', mohlát 'deadline'); enclitic/affixal morphemes can shift the accent with vowel reduction (2019 §4).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress as transcribed in Häberl's Khorramshahr corpus (elicited words and running text); 2019 examples explicitly 'reflect the Khorramshahr dialect'; 2025 adds that Ahvaz and Khorramshahr dialects are mutually intelligible. Tense vowels lengthen in open accented syllables, so length is a correlate not a determinant.
new_statements.identity_note: Both quoted statements are by the primary modern describer (Häberl) and rest on his Khorramshahr-dialect corpus (speaker Nasser Sobbi); the 2019 chapter says 'These transcriptions reflect the Khorramshahr dialect' and the 2025 chapter states the Ahvaz and Khorramshahr dialects are mutually intelligible. Glottolog nucl1706 'Neo-Mandaic' covers both; no separate glottocodes for the two dialects are known to me. Häberl 2019 titles the chapter simply 'Mandaic' but explicitly means the vernacular ('Neo-Mandaic' / 'Modern Mandaic', ISO mid), not Classical Mandaic (clas1252).

sources.note: §3 Phonology, p. 687: word stress falls on a tense vowel in a closed syllable, computed from the final syllable: closed+tense ultima is stressed; otherwise penult if closed or tense-vowelled; otherwise final; in 3+-syllable words with neither ultima nor penult qualifying, stress recedes to the antepenult; negative lá- and some other morphemes attract stress. Transcriptions reflect the Khorramshahr dialect.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Neo-Mandaic', section Phonology > Stress (retrieved 2026-09-17 via API).
sources.note: Second-hand (based on Häberl 2009): same algorithm — accent on tense vowel in closed syllable, determined from the ultima; closed+tense ultima stressed (farwɔh [fær.ˈwɔh]); else penult if closed or tense (gawrɔ [ˈgæv.rɔ]); else final (əxal [a.ˈχɑl]); antepenult in 3+ syllable words (gaṭelnɔxon); lá- attracts accent.

sources.note: §3.0 Transcription System, pp. 747-748: 'I indicate word stress only when it cannot be predicted. Generally, it falls upon a tense vowel within a closed syllable, and its placement is conditioned by the final syllable. Any final syllable that is closed and contains a tense vowel automatically receives the stress, e.g., Baġdɔ́d... If the final is either open or contains a lax vowel, then the stress falls on the penultimate syllable in words of two syllables, e.g., éṯmal, ṣɔ́tni, or the antepenultimate syllable in words of three or more syllables, e.g., gaṭélnɔxon, provided that either syllable…
